title: Tracking the same wave crest
stem:
A video follows the same crest of a travelling wave. Simulated positions are listed below; the uncertainty of every position is ±0.005 m and timing uncertainty is negligible. The wavelength is measured independently as 0.24 m.

| Time / s | Crest position / m |
|---:|---:|
| 0.00 | 0.100 |
| 0.05 | 0.200 |
| 0.10 | 0.300 |
| 0.15 | 0.400 |

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Estimate the maximum absolute uncertainty in this endpoint speed.

parts.label: c

steps.text: Use the slope of crest position against time.
Uncertainty in the position difference is 2Δx = 0.01 m.
Δv = 2Δx/Δt = 0.05 m s⁻¹.
The camera follows a propagating phase feature. Individual medium particles oscillate locally instead of travelling along with that crest.

title: Refraction and critical conditions
stem: A ray enters glass of refractive index 1.5 from air at 38° to the normal. What is its refracted angle?

verification.method: Deterministic calculation, wave-boundary and dimensional checks in the independent authoring script
verification.notes: Editorial family C13; variant 1/4. Original setting, numbers, data and artwork; analytical solution and marking arithmetic checked by author. Independent editorial review is separate.

steps.text: A. Snell’s law gives sin θ₂ = sin 38°/1.5, so θ₂ = 24.2°. The ray bends toward the normal.

subject: physics-hl
title: Refraction and critical conditions
stem: Light travels from water of refractive index 1.33 toward air. What is the critical angle measured inside the water?

verification.method: Deterministic calculation, wave-boundary and dimensional checks in the independent authoring script
verification.notes: Editorial family C13; variant 2/4. Original setting, numbers, data and artwork; analytical solution and marking arithmetic checked by author. Independent editorial review is separate.

steps.text: B. At critical incidence the transmitted ray is at 90° to the normal. Thus sin $\theta_{\mathrm{c}}$ = 1/1.33 and $\theta_{\mathrm{c}}$ = 48.8°.

subject: physics-hl
title: Refraction and critical conditions
stem: Which set of conditions allows total internal reflection at a transparent boundary?

verification.method: Deterministic calculation, wave-boundary and dimensional checks in the independent authoring script
verification.notes: Editorial family C13; variant 3/4. Original setting, numbers, data and artwork; analytical solution and marking arithmetic checked by author. Independent editorial review is separate.

options.label: A
options.text: The light is normally incident from any medium.

options.label: B
options.text: The incidence angle equals zero and both media have the same index.

options.label: C
options.text: The incident medium has higher refractive index and incidence exceeds the critical angle.

options.label: D
options.text: The incident medium has lower refractive index and incidence exceeds 45°.

steps.text: C. Total internal reflection requires travel toward a lower-index medium and incidence greater than the relevant critical angle.

title: Refraction and critical conditions
stem: A ray entering a transparent material from air has incidence 50.0° and refraction 30.0°, both measured from the normal. What is the material’s refractive index?

verification.notes: Editorial family C13; variant 4/4. Original setting, numbers, data and artwork; analytical solution and marking arithmetic checked by author. Independent editorial review is separate.

steps.text: D. With air index 1, n = sin 50.0°/sin 30.0° = 1.53. Ratios of angles themselves are not Snell’s law.

subject: physics-hl
title: A half-integer path difference
stem: Two coherent sources oscillate in phase. At point P their path difference is 2.5 wavelengths and their amplitudes are equal. What is observed at P?

verification.method: Deterministic calculation, wave-boundary and dimensional checks in the independent authoring script
verification.notes: Editorial family C14; variant 1/4. Original setting, numbers, data and artwork; analytical solution and marking arithmetic checked by author. Independent editorial review is separate.

options.label: C
options.text: A permanent doubling of the wave frequency.

options.label: D
options.text: No superposition because the sources are separate.

steps.text: A. A half-integer number of wavelengths gives a phase difference of an odd multiple of π. Equal-amplitude displacements cancel.

subject: physics-hl
title: An integer path difference
stem: Two coherent sources oscillate in phase and have equal amplitude A at P. Their path difference is three wavelengths. What is the resultant amplitude at P?

verification.method: Deterministic calculation, wave-boundary and dimensional checks in the independent authoring script
verification.notes: Editorial family C14; variant 2/4. Original setting, numbers, data and artwork; analytical solution and marking arithmetic checked by author. Independent editorial review is separate.

steps.text: B. An integer path difference gives in-phase arrival. The displacements add, so the resultant amplitude is 2A.

subject: physics-hl
title: Two overlapping pulses
stem: At one point, two small transverse pulses would separately produce displacements +0.035 m and −0.020 m. What displacement does linear superposition predict?

verification.method: Deterministic calculation, wave-boundary and dimensional checks in the independent authoring script
verification.notes: Editorial family C14; variant 3/4. Original setting, numbers, data and artwork; analytical solution and marking arithmetic checked by author. Independent editorial review is separate.

steps.text: C. Add signed displacements: +0.035 − 0.020 = +0.015 m. The signs describe opposite directions.

subject: physics-hl
title: Conditions for a stable pattern
stem: Which property of two sources is essential for a stable interference pattern?

verification.method: Deterministic calculation, wave-boundary and dimensional checks in the independent authoring script
verification.notes: Editorial family C14; variant 4/4. Original setting, numbers, data and artwork; analytical solution and marking arithmetic checked by author. Independent editorial review is separate.

options.label: A
options.text: Exactly equal source powers in every circumstance.

options.label: C
options.text: Both sources moving at the wave speed.

options.label: D
options.text: A constant phase difference and the same frequency.

steps.text: D. Coherence requires a stable phase relation. Equal amplitude improves contrast but is not the defining requirement for a stable pattern.

title: Designing a two-slit measurement
stem: Normally incident monochromatic light of vacuum wavelength 450 nm passes through two narrow slits separated by 0.2 mm. A screen is 1.5 m away in air. Use the small-angle approximation, with air refractive index 1.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the separation of adjacent bright fringes.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Determine the distance from the central bright fringe to the order-2 bright fringe on one side.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The whole space between slits and screen is filled with a transparent medium of refractive index 1.2. Predict the new fringe spacing and explain which wave quantity stays unchanged.

steps.text: Use s = λD/d, converting wavelength and slit separation to metres.

The frequency stays fixed because it is set by the source; speed and wavelength both decrease in the medium.

subject: physics-hl
title: Checking a common spectral-line shift
stem:
Three identified emission lines from one source are measured in a calibrated spectrum as follows. All listed values are simulated. Adopt positive radial velocity for recession and c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. Use the low-speed Doppler approximation.

| Laboratory wavelength / nm | Observed wavelength / nm |
|---:|---:|
| 400 | 400.400 |
| 500 | 500.500 |
| 650 | 650.650 |

verification.method: Deterministic calculation, wave-boundary and dimensional checks in the independent authoring script
verification.notes: Editorial family C30; variant 1/4. Original setting, numbers, data and artwork; analytical solution and marking arithmetic checked by author. Independent editorial review is separate.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the fractional wavelength shift for each line and assess whether one radial velocity can explain them.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Determine the radial velocity, including its direction.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Predict the observed wavelength of an additional line whose laboratory wavelength is 580 nm.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Explain why the approximation used is appropriate for these data.

steps.text: For each line calculate z = ($\lambda_{\mathrm{observed}}$ − $\lambda_{\mathrm{rest}}$)/$\lambda_{\mathrm{rest}}$.
All three give z = 0.001, consistent with a common radial velocity.
$v_{\mathrm{radial}}$ ≈ cz = 3e+05 m s⁻¹, indicating recession.
$\lambda_{\mathrm{observed}}$ = $\lambda_{\mathrm{rest}}$(1 + z) = 580.58 nm.
|v|/c ≈ |z| = 0.001, which is much less than one, so relativistic corrections are small.
